brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.

requirements.requirement: Herb planter of three cells side by side
requirements.evidence: Three full-depth hex pieces at axial (-1,0), (0,0), (1,0) on level 0, a straight line of adjacent cells, joined by two joint bolts (0,0 slot 0 and slot 3). check_build shows meshClash clear and no LOOSE_BODY warning.

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a bin that drains
requirements.evidence: Each cell holds a hex-bin-full-drain (drained, full depth) bin: bin:-1,0,0, bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0. Each is filled with soil and planted (basil, flat-leaf parsley, chives). Drainage is shown by the drained bin geometry; I have not verified water flow or material.
Soil filled in all three bins and a herb plug plant set in each; no PLANT_NOT_IN_SOIL or prop warnings.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell herb planter: three full-depth hex pieces in a straight row, each with a drained full-depth bin, joined by two joint bolts, soil-filled and planted with basil, parsley and chives. check_build is clean (meshClash clear, no errors). Drainage is the bin's drained geometry only; material and waterproofing are not verified.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
